verdicts.evidence: Green on a clean diff ('No credentials in the diff - Scanned 2 files for tokens, keys and kubeconfigs' on base, 'Scanned 0 files' on a clean demo, 'Scanned 7 files' with seven changed). Drove the positive case: wrote /app/pkg/demo/w6-check-probe.ts containing a ghp_-shaped string, and the row turned red and read '2 possible credentials in the diff - Scanned 7 files for tokens, keys and kubeconfigs. barn-review-w6.vue:2 looks like a GitHub personal access token; w6-check-probe.ts:2 looks like a GitHub personal access token.' It named file and line and never echoed what it matched. Probe file removed afterwards.

Green state is right ('No unstable Kubernetes APIs added - The added lines name no alpha or beta group-version'). Drove the warning state by putting `metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1` into a file in the demo pod's tree. The row did turn to the alert glyph, it did not gate (Publish stayed enabled and read 'Publish to 1 place' beside it) - but the sentence rendered as: 'Uses an unstable API. undefined (barn-review-w6.vue:3). An alpha or beta group-version can change or disappear between Kubernetes minors...'. The group-version is printed as the literal word 'undefined'.
verdicts.defect: PublishModal.vue's `unstableCheck()` builds its sentence with `this.unstable.map((f) => `${f.api} (${f.path}:${f.line})`)` (pkg/barn/components/PublishModal.vue:790), but `scanUnstableApis()` returns `Finding` objects whose field is `what`, not `api` (pkg/barn/change-checks.ts:23-28 and :191). So the one thing the row exists to tell you - which group-version is unstable - is always 'undefined'. The credentials row two lines above uses `f.what` correctly, and screen 12's automated-checks column also uses `f.what` (pages/review-change.vue:3200), so this is the single wrong field reference. The check has only ever been seen green before, which is why it read as a pass.

verdicts.defect: Not a defect in the code path. Blocked on a GitHub credential this environment does not have.

verdicts.evidence: The dialog is headed 'Import an extension from GitHub' and the caption under it reads 'The repository is cloned into your workspace. Nothing is pushed back until you publish.' - both present in the first-run state and in the connected state.

On /dashboard/barn/extensions the title row carries a neutral 'Import' button with a github glyph beside 'New extension'. Clicking it opened the modal titled 'Import an extension from GitHub' over the list, with the URL unchanged.

With the modal open, the Studio table was still rendered behind it (.studio-home__table present with its rows) and location.href was still https://magic-closet-rancher/dashboard/barn/extensions - no navigation happened.

'Name in Studio' came up prefilled from the repository - 'kubewarden-ui' - with the hint 'Taken from the repository. Change it to call it something else here.' Typing 'W6 Probe Name' changed the hint to 'It will be called w6-probe-name.' (it normalises rather than rejects), and typing 'base' produced the error 'base already exists here.' and disabled Import. It is a free-text field, not the select the chevron in the mock suggests, which is the right call for a name.

There is no separate 'Not listed? Paste a repository URL instead' link, because the escape hatch is the field itself and it says so: with no list its hint reads 'Name the one you want, or paste its URL.' Pasted https://github.com/rancher/kubewarden-ui/tree/main and the hint became 'Reads as rancher/kubewarden-ui.', the branch defaulted to main from the URL, and the pre-import check ran against it. Typing 'not a repo!!' produced 'That has to be owner/name, or a github.com repository URL.'

It inspects the chosen repo and branch from a pod and has three answers, not one. rancher/kubewarden-ui@main: green - 'This looks like a Rancher extension. Found pkg/kubewarden/package.json, pkg/kubewarden/index.ts, a pkg/ directory and the rancher annotations block. It asks for Rancher >= 2.11.0-0, and this Rancher is 2.15.' - which is the marker files and the version skew the design asks for. octocat/Hello-World: amber - 'This does not look like a Rancher extension. Did not find package.json, index.ts, a pkg/ directory and the rancher annotations block. You can import it anyway, and the assistant will have to make an extension of it.' rancher/definitely-not-real-w6-probe: grey - 'Studio could not see it on GitHub. It may be private, in which case connect GitHub in step 1 and the import will still work even though this check cannot see it. Otherwise the name is wrong.' None of the three gates Import, which matches the frame (Import is drawn fully enabled beside a passing check).

The rows the lock/book glyph and the relative updated time belong to are rendered from `listGithubRepos`, which the pod runs with the stored token. With a token GitHub rejects, the list comes back empty and the panel says so instead of drawing rows: 'GitHub rejected the token (Bad credentials). Name the repository below or paste its URL instead.' So there is no row to read the visibility or the updated time off. Needs a credential GitHub accepts; not fabricated.
verdicts.defect: Needs a valid GitHub token to verify. No code defect observed - the failure is reported honestly.

verdicts.evidence: Same cause: `barn-import-repo-list` is only rendered when the pod's listing returns rows, and with a token GitHub rejects it returns none. There is nothing to click, so the highlight, the check glyph and the single-select behaviour cannot be driven. What is verifiable is the other half of the same state, and it holds: typing owner/name into the field below is the path the product keeps working without a list, and the field's hint says so.
verdicts.defect: Needs a valid GitHub token to verify.

verdicts.evidence: The search box is deliberately only drawn when there is a list to search (`v-if="repos.length"`), and with a token GitHub rejects there is none - `barn-import-repo-search` was absent in both the no-token and the rejected-token states. So the filtering cannot be driven either way.
verdicts.defect: Needs a valid GitHub token to verify.

verdicts.evidence: With the modal open a full-viewport scrim covers the page (the .s-modal root paints rgba(0,0,0,0.45) over the whole 1440x900 viewport) and the Studio list behind it is dimmed. Clicking it dismissed the dialog - an exit the design does not draw, alongside the Cancel and close icon it does.

Three stacked steps, all visible at once, with 22px round markers that carry the state. Unconnected: step 1 is a blue disc (rgb(61,152,211) = #3D98D3) with a '1', steps 2 and 3 are flat grey (rgb(240,241,244)) with grey digits. Connected: step 1 becomes a solid green (rgb(62,140,79) = #3E8C4F) disc with a check glyph and the heading changes to 'GitHub connected', and steps 2 and 3 both turn blue and open for input. Watched both transitions happen.

Everything up to the press is verified: with rancher/kubewarden-ui@main chosen and the pre-import check green, the green primary Import button went from disabled/0.4 opacity to enabled/1.0 opacity, and it went back to disabled the moment the name collided with an existing extension. The press itself I did not make. It provisions a seed ConfigMap, a node:24 Deployment and a Service in the shared `barn` namespace and runs a multi-minute install, in a cluster where several other verifiers' pods are working right now - and the promise's payload (the extension appears in the Studio list with a GitHub source of owner/repo and the chosen branch) cannot be read without it. Worth noting the blocker here is the shared cluster rather than a credential: a public repository clones with no token at all, which is the point of the 'carry on without connecting' path.
verdicts.defect: The clone itself is unverified. Not a credential problem for a public repository.

verdicts.evidence: No 'Authorise with GitHub' button anywhere in step 1. Step 1 says why, in the copy itself: 'There is no "Authorise with GitHub" because Studio has no OAuth app of its own to send you to.'
verdicts.defect: Deliberate and stated on screen. OAuth needs a client id and a callback, and this product has no server for either. The token field is the whole of step 1 and the copy admits it rather than drawing a button that opens nothing.

verdicts.evidence: With barn-settings empty, opened the wizard and clicked the footer Cancel: it was at full opacity and enabled (unlike Import beside it at 0.4), the modal closed, and barn-settings still had no data and no token annotation afterwards.
Same unconnected state: clicked the X in the head, the modal closed, no extension was created and barn-settings was still empty (no `gh_token` key, no `barn.rancher.io/gh-token` annotation).

Step 1 is headed 'Connect GitHub' and its paragraph reads 'Studio clones the repository from a pod in this cluster, which takes a few seconds and happens without leaving this dialog. A public repository needs nothing at all. A private one needs a token, and you can paste it here without losing what you have typed. There is no "Authorise with GitHub" because Studio has no OAuth app of its own to send you to.' It says what the access is for, that it is quick, and that you are not navigated away - and it goes one better by saying a public repository needs no access at all.

With no token stored, clicking Import on the Studio list opened the same modal - same title 'Import an extension from GitHub', same caption 'The repository is cloned into your workspace. Nothing is pushed back until you publish.', over the same list, with location.href unchanged. No redirect to a settings page.

In the unconnected state the Import button is disabled=true and computed opacity 0.4; clicking it did nothing and the modal stayed open. It is the same button that reached opacity 1 and disabled=false later, once a repository was chosen and the check had run. The gate is real, not only visual: `disabled` is set, so it is announced to assistive technology too, which the design's opacity-only treatment would not be.

Unconnected: step 1's marker is a blue disc, computed background rgb(61,152,211) (#3D98D3), with a white '1'; steps 2 and 3 are rgb(240,241,244) with grey digits. After connecting, step 1's marker became rgb(62,140,79) (#3E8C4F) with a check glyph and steps 2 and 3 both became rgb(61,152,211). Both halves of the promise observed.

Before connecting, step 2 and step 3 render with data-state="locked", grey markers and grey headings, and their content is swapped rather than dimmed: step 3's content is empty, and step 2's is a single sentence - 'Locked until GitHub is connected. A public repository needs no token, so carry on without connecting if the one you want is public.' No search box, no repository list, no branch control and no name control exist in the DOM at all, so there is nothing focusable behind the lock. The escape hatch in that sentence is the product's own addition and it works: clicking it opened both steps.

Step 1 draws a 'Paste a personal access token' link at the end of its copy; the token panel is collapsed until it is clicked. Clicking it revealed the labelled field, the help text and a 'Connect' button, and the link itself disappeared (it is a one-way disclosure). There is no Authorise button beside it, for the reason step 1 gives.

Inside the disclosure: a labelled 'Personal access token' field, type=password so the value is masked, placeholder 'ghp_...', set in a monospace face (computed font-family '"JetBrains Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace'). It has an explicit Connect button, which the design leaves undrawn - Connect is disabled until something is typed and enabled after. Submitting a token did unlock steps 2 and 3 (step 1 went to the green 'GitHub connected' state), which is the second half of the promise.

Under the field: 'Needs the repo scope only. Create one on GitHub with the scope pre-selected. It is stored in a Secret in this Rancher, not in your browser, because the thing that spends it is a pod - which also means it is shared with everyone using this Rancher's Studio, not held per user.' The pre-selected-scopes route is a real anchor, href https://github.com/settings/tokens/new?scopes=repo&description=Rancher%20Extension%20Studio, so the gap the feature note flags (plain caption text with nothing to click) is closed. The storage promise deliberately contradicts the design's 'stored per user': it is one Secret in the barn namespace, shared, and the copy says so instead of promising something the product does not do. Confirmed against the cluster - the token I stored briefly landed in the single `barn-settings` Secret and was visible to the whole Studio.
